page: Vultr voc-s-8c-64gb-1920s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes a 32 MB L3 cache and supports key instruction sets such as AVX, AES, SHA_NI, and BMI2. The hardware configuration is bundled with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU, and includes a local 1920 GB NVMe SSD for high-speed storage.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance ranking in the top tier (top 10%). Multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth tests, including both cached and uncached read/write operations, consistently place in the average tier. Text processing workloads show strong performance in the top 25% of tested systems. However, complex computational tasks such as medium-sized LLM prompt processing (7B model) show weaker performance, placing in the bottom 25%, while text generation for the same model remains average.

This server offers a balanced qualitative cost profile for memory-intensive and storage-heavy workloads due to its high resource density, combining 64 GB of RAM with a substantial 1920 GB NVMe SSD. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures predictable execution times without resource contention. It is well-suited for database hosting, memory-cached web serving, text processing pipelines, and moderate enterprise applications that require a combination of dedicated compute resources, high memory capacity, and fast local storage.
